Label: taxonomic class assertion
Description: An assertion that holds between an ontology class and an organism taxon class, which is intepreted to yield some relationship between instances of the ontology class and the taxon. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: phenotype of
Description: inverse of has phenotype Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has gene product
Description: x has gene product y if and only if x is a gene (SO:0000704) that participates in some gene expression process (GO:0010467) where the output of that process is either y or something that is ribosomally translated from y Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: expressed in
Description: x expressed in y if and only if there is a gene expression process (GO:0010467) that occurs in y, and one of the following holds: (i) x is a gene, and x is transcribed into a transcript as part of the gene expression process (ii) x is a transcript, and the transcription of x is part of the gene expression process (iii) x is a mature gene product such as a protein, and x was translated or otherwise processes from a transcript that was transcribed as part of this gene expression process Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: parasitoid of
Description: A parasite that kills or sterilizes its host Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has parasitoid
Description: inverse of parasitoid of Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has prototype
Description: x has prototype y if and only if x is an instance of C and y is a prototypical instance of C. For example, every instance of heart, both normal and abnormal is related by the has prototype relation to some instance of a "canonical" heart, which participates in blood circulation. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: obsolete actively participates in

Label: obsolete has active participant
Description: OBSOLETE x has participant y if and only if x realizes some active role that inheres in y Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: obligate parasite of
Description: A sub-relation of parasite-of in which the parasite that cannot complete its life cycle without a host. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: facultative parasite of
Description: A sub-relations of parasite-of in which the parasite that can complete its life cycle independent of a host. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: stem parasite of

Label: root parasite of
Description: A parasite-of relationship in which the host is a plant and the parasite that attaches to the host root (PO:0009005) Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: hemiparasite of
Description: A sub-relation of parasite-of in which the parasite is a plant, and the parasite is parasitic under natural conditions and is also photosynthetic to some degree. Hemiparasites may just obtain water and mineral nutrients from the host plant. Many obtain at least part of their organic nutrients from the host as well. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has component participant
Description: X 'has component participant' Y means X 'has participant' Y and there is a cardinality constraint that specifies the numbers of Ys. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has exposure receptor
Description: A broad relationship between an exposure event or process and any entity (e.g., an organism, organism population, or an organism part) that interacts with an exposure stimulus during the exposure event. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has exposure stressor
Description: A broad relationship between an exposure event or process and any agent, stimulus, activity, or event that causes stress or tension on an organism and interacts with an exposure receptor during an exposure event. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: over-expressed in
Description: g is over-expressed in t iff g is expressed in t, and the expression level of g is increased relative to some background. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: under-expressed in
Description: g is under-expressed in t iff g is expressed in t, and the expression level of g is decreased relative to some background. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has active ingredient
Description: A relationship that holds between a substance and a chemical entity, if the chemical entity is part of the substance, and the chemical entity forms the biologically active component of the substance. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: active ingredient in

Label: evolutionary variant of
Description: Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: transports or maintains localization of
Description: Holds between p and c when p is a localization process (localization covers maintenance of localization as well as its establishment) and the outcome of this process is to regulate the localization of c. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: colocalizes with
Description: a colocalizes_with b if and only if a is transiently or peripherally associated with b[GO]. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: contributes to
Description: Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: enables

Description: inverse of enables Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: negatively regulated by
Description: inverse of negatively regulates Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: positively regulated by
Description: inverse of positively regulates Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: imports

Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: exports
Description: Holds between p and c when p is a transportation or localization process and the outcome of this process is to move c to a destination that is part of some s, where the end location of c is part of the region that surrounds s. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: results in developmental induction of
Description: p results in developmental induction of c if and only if p is a collection of cell-cell signaling processes that signal to a neighbouring tissue that is the precursor of the mature c, where the signaling results in the commitment to cell types necessary for the formation of c. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: anabranch of
Description: x anabranch_of y if x is a distributary of y (i.e. it channels a from a larger flow from y) and x ultimately channels the flow back into y. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: spatially coextensive with
Description: x spatially_coextensive_with y if and inly if x and y have the same location Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: main stem of
Description: x main_stem_of y if y is a branching structure and x is a channel that traces a linear path through y, such that x has higher capacity than any other such path. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: proper distributary of

Label: proper tributary of

Label: has potential to developmentally induce

Label: obsolete has direct output

Label: obsolete has indirect output
Description: Likely to be obsoleted. See: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1QMhs9J-P_q3o_rDh-IX4ZEnz0PnXrzLRVkI3vvz8NEQ/edit Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: causally downstream of
Description: inverse of upstream of Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Description: Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: obsolete directly inhibits
Description: This term was obsoleted because it has the same meaning as 'directly negatively regulates'. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: provides input for

Label: transitively provides input for
Description: transitive form of directly_provides_input_for Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: co-roosts with
Description: Two or more individuals sharing the same roost site (cave, mine, tree or tree hollow, animal burrow, leaf tent, rock crack, space in man-made structure, etc.). Individuals that are sharing a communal roost may be said to be co-roosting. The roost may be either a day roost where the individuals rest during daytime hours, or a night roost where individuals roost to feed, groom, or rest in between flights and/or foraging bouts. Communal roosting as thus defined is an umbrella term within which different specialized types -- which are not mutually exclusive -- may be recognized based on taxonomy and the temporal and spatial relationships of the individuals that are co-roosting. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: reservoir host of

Some zoonotic pathogens, particularly bacterial pathogens, may also have environmental reservoirs. Microorganisms with multiple reservoir species may be indefinitely maintained across the community of species even if they are not always present in each individual reservoir species. In the reservoir species or community, the microorganism may cause either asymptomatic infection or disease and this may vary among individuals. A pathogen may also be more genetically diverse in its reservoir host than in other taxa, in part because the pathogen is endemic to reservoir hosts. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

The causal relations in this hierarchy can be used in linking either physical or abstract genetic variations to phenotypes or diseases they cause or contribute to. Environmental exposures include those imposed by natural environments, experimentally applied conditions, or clinical interventions. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: has epiphyte

Label: kleptoparasitized by
Description: inverse of kleptoparasite of Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: creates habitat for
Description: An interaction relationship wherein one organism creates a structure or environment that is lived in by another organism. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: ecologically co-occurs with
Description: An interaction relationship describing organisms that often occur together at the same time and space or in the same environment. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: lays eggs on

Label: has eggs laid on by

Label: trophic parasite of

Label: has primary substance added

Label: assay measures characteristic

Label: regulates quantity of

Label: indirectly regulates activity of

Label: decreases by repression quantity of

Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: increases by expression quantity of

The up-regulation is due to A having an effect on an intermediate entity (typically a DNA or mRNA element) which can produce B. For example, protein A (transcription factor) indirectly increases by expression the quantity of protein B (gene product) if and only if A positively regulates the process of transcription or translation of a nucleic acid element that produces B. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: directly positively regulates quantity of

Label: directly negatively regulates quantity of
Description: The entity A has an activity that directly negatively regulates the quantity of B. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: indirectly positively regulates activity of
Description: The entity A is not immediately upstream of the entity B and has an activity that up-regulates an activity performed by B. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: destabilizes quantity of

Label: stabilizes quantity of

Label: indirectly negatively regulates activity of

Label: directly regulates quantity of

Label: indirectly regulates quantity of

Label: indirectly negatively regulates quantity of
Description: The entity A does not physically interact with the entity B, and A has an activity that down-regulates the quantity or abundance or concentration of B. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: indirectly positively regulates quantity of
Description: The entity A does not physically interact with the entity B, and A has an activity that up-regulates the quantity or abundance or concentration of B. Declared in the schema but used in no triple or class axiom.

Label: in convergence relationship with

Label: in structural homology relationship with

Label: in reversal relationship with

Label: in syntenic homology relationship with

Label: in paralogy relationship with

Label: in syntenic paralogy relationship with

Label: in partial homology relationship with

Label: obsolete reciprocal_of
Description: Refer to https://github.com/pato-ontology/pato/issues/454. There are frequently two ways to state the same thing: we can say 'spermatocyte lacks asters' or 'asters absent from spermatocyte'. In this case the quality is 'lacking all parts of type' - it is a (relational) quality of the spermatocyte, and it is with respect to instances of 'aster'. One of the popular requirements of PATO is that it continue to support 'absent', so we need to relate statements which use this quality to the 'lacking all parts of type' quality.
